title: Soma passes beyond the purifying filter

words.context: Bhāskara explains it as the knower of the sacrifices
Bhāskara: «स्वधितिः अग्निः», and others take it as a great tree

sandhi.rule: m before p is written as the class nasal (here m)
m joins the following vowel; -iḥ before a voiced sound becomes -ir
m joins the vowel; i before a dissimilar vowel becomes y

morphology.note: a nominative in -īḥ of the root-noun type (pada-vī, ‘who goes to the place’); Bhāskara discusses the form.

translation.literal: Brahman-priest among the gods, path-finder among poets, seer among the inspired, buffalo among wild beasts, falcon among birds of prey, axe among the trees: Soma passes beyond the filter, singing.
translation.readable: Among the gods the priest, among poets the path-finder, among the inspired the seer, the buffalo among beasts, the falcon among hunting birds, the axe among the trees — Soma runs on through the filter, singing.

meaning: A praise of Soma by comparisons: as the brahman priest is first among gods, the seer among the inspired, the falcon among birds of prey, so Soma, singing, passes through the purifying filter and surpasses all that purifies. In the Navagraha sūktam it is the second mantra for Ketu; the witness names the graha’s adhidevatā and pratyadhidevatā together, without saying which mantra is whose.
in_the_rite: Step 9 (Ketu), second mantra. The use of a Vedic verse for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition; the commentary below speaks of the verse in its Vedic setting. In the Saṃhitā (TS 3.4.11.1) it is a yājyā of the Rājasūya offerings, as Bhāskara’s introduction says; it is also RV 9.96.6.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara introduces it as a yājyā, «तत्रैव याज्या», and reads the comparisons: «देवानां मध्ये ब्रह्मा सोमः ब्रह्मात्मना वर्तते»; so Soma, among all that purifies, goes beyond: «एवं सोमः पवित्राणां मध्ये पवित्रमत्येति».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: A triṣṭubh. The Taittirīya and the Ṛgveda (9.96.6) have the same words.
